findings.summary: The demonstrated scope refusal is supported, but exact target membership and delivery do not make review purpose redundant.
evidence: Counterexample: an honestly scoped causal-review packet names the exact issues. Its delivered observations pass the diagnostic question, summarize confirmation of the root cause, and cite failing reproductions. No repair exists. All packet/result targets and delivery identities match. The current prefix check refuses this carrier; the proposed structured exemption removes that refusal although the review approved diagnosis, not resolution.
issue_worker_targets.py validates exact membership, passing verdicts, and nonempty summaries/evidence. It does not distinguish a passing diagnostic judgment from a passing resolution judgment.
closeout-carrier.md explicitly states that the delivered causal review approves diagnosis, not design or resolution, and that a release-state review alone does not prove issue behavior.

reviewer_worker_carrier.py checks required_scope_prefix separately from identity and delivery validation. Preserving scope equality across delivery joins preserves what was reviewed; it does not establish eligibility for a different consuming purpose.

baseline.json supports the observed producer/consumer mismatch through a deterministic backend fixture. Its explicit absence of model judgment means it cannot establish semantic redundancy of the purpose check.
findings.action: Revise the repair hypothesis to preserve a resolution-purpose distinction. Cross-format reuse can remain valid when the issue owner establishes that actual observations cover resolution claims; structured presence and mechanical validation alone are insufficient. Test the causal-only counterexample alongside the positive arbitrary-label case before approving a repair.
